prompt: Build a generic LIFO stack backed by an ArrayList. Complete push, pop, peek, isEmpty, and size in GenericStack<T>; pop and peek return null when the stack is empty.
explanation: A generic class declares a type parameter <T> once and uses it for every element method, so one implementation works for String, Integer, or any other type. Backing the stack with an ArrayList makes the end of the list the top of the stack, so push is add, and pop removes at index size() - 1. Returning null for pop/peek on an empty stack avoids an IndexOutOfBoundsException.
hints: Treat the END of the ArrayList as the top: push is items.add(item).
The top item lives at index items.size() - 1; pop uses items.remove(...) and peek uses items.get(...).
In pop and peek, first test items.isEmpty() and return null in that case.
